newsitem.title: USA: SF Fed's Parry sees sustainable U.S. growth--CNBC.
newsitem.headline: SF Fed's Parry sees sustainable U.S. growth--CNBC.

text.p: The U.S. economy has performed unusually well, paving the way for annual growth rates of between 2.0 and 2.5 percent over the next year or more, said the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco.
"The economy has performed extraordinarily well," Robert Parry, the San Franciso Fed chief, told the CNBC network on Monday.
"My own view is that over the next year, or perhaps even longer, we're probably going to see growth at about 2.0 to 2.5 percent," he added.
Parry said he thought those rates of growth to be "reasonably sustainable."
The San Francisco Fed chief said growth in the third quarter of 1997 may be somewhat faster than in the second quarter, when the economy expanded at a 2.2 percent rate.
But Parry, who sits at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and is scheduled to vote on policy actions in 1997, warned that it was too soon to draw conclusions based on early third quarter data.
"It certainly is possible that we'll see growth in the third quarter that is faster than we saw in the second," Parry said.
"But I would caution you that the monthly statistics about the economy have a tendency to ebb and flow," he added.

On Friday, the Labor Department released its July employment report, which showed a stronger-than-expected growth in non-farmn payrolls and a drop in the jobless rate to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June.
Also on Friday, the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) reported its manufacturing index jumped to 58.6 in July against 55.7 in June.
Parry also said U.S. inflation appeared well-behaved.
He said, however, that the risks for higher inflation rested largely on possible wage pressures.

"If problems begin to show up, they'll probably show up in terms of an accelaration in the wage and compensation costs, but we really haven't seen much there that would indicate a problem," Parry said.
